Definition: of uncertain origin; Lystra, a place in Asia Minor:--Lystra.
BiblicalUsage: Lystra was a city of Lycaonia where Paul healed a man crippled from his mother's womb, and where the crowd first hailed him as a god and then stoned him and dragged him out of the city. Paul returned there on his second journey and found Timothy, a disciple whose mother was a Jewess and whose father was a Greek, and Timothy became his fellow worker from that day.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Lystra holds both the best and worst of ministry in one place: a miracle, a stoning, and a young man called to carry the gospel on.
